title: Market explained
description: India has opened its stock market wider to individual investors living abroad. Earlier, only Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs).

faq.q: Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) still invest in Indian stocks?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs) were already permitted to invest in listed Indian companies, and they continue to be able to do so. This new rule simply expands the definition to include all individuals residing outside India.
Equity instruments primarily refer to shares of a company, which represent ownership. When you buy equity instruments, you become a part-owner of the company.

"Repatriation basis" means that the foreign investor is allowed to take their initial investment amount and any profits or capital gains earned from that investment back to their home country in foreign currency.

faq.q: Are there any restrictions on which Indian companies foreign individuals can invest in?
faq.a: Yes, investments are subject to prohibited activities and sectoral caps as prescribed under the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules. For instance, certain sectors might have limits on foreign investment.

faq.q: Will this affect the value of the Indian Rupee?
faq.a: The government hopes that increased foreign capital inflows due to these changes will help strengthen the Indian Rupee and stabilize the capital account, especially during times of global economic volatility.
